description.narrative: OPIC has presented to Sida a proposal for support to civil society organizations in Kosovo for the period 2016-2020, indicating greater focus on labor rights, gender equality, the empowerment of underrepresented groups and anti-corruption. This concept makes the added value of OPIC clearer, and it is evidently in line with their core activities in Sweden. The programmatic content of the project document coherent with the current program for Kosovo 2012-2015. The required total budget is 25 000 000 SEK.

Olof Palme International Center har presenterat ett förslag till Sida för insats till stöd till civilsamhällesorganisationer i Kosovo under perioden 2016-2020. Jämfört med tidigare stöd innebär förslaget ett större fokus på arbetstagares och underrepresenterade gruppers rättigheter, jämställdhet, samt antikorruption. Förslaget korresponderar därmed väl med Olof Palme International Centers kärnaktiviteter i Sverige som ökar mervärdet av insatsen. Projektet är i övrigt i enlighet med Olof Palme International Centers tidigare projekt för 2012-2015. Budgeten för projektet är 25 000 000 SEK.

The OPIC programme objective is "To see citizens, in particular women and youth, and other civil society groups be actively involved in local organisations/or networks and take an active role in governance by influencing the policies, political agendas and decisions in their favour". The OPC strategy for the Kosovo programme is focused on the following main areas of work: a) citizen participation in decision-making, b) transparency and accountability, c) socio-economic and labour rights, d) support to progressive political parties and movements. OPIC theory of change " The social transformation and development is achieved through collective organising" is valid and applicable. All reporting requirements as per the ageement conditions are met. Annual audit report is clean and no deviation from the annual work plan is reported.

he OPC program in 2022 continued to focus on supporting local organizations that build a vibrant civil society and thus promote democratic consolidation focused on three main themes: citizen participation, labor and socio-economic rights, and transparency and accountability. Although the OPC remained focused on consolidating existing coalitions, it also included new partners aiming to form strategic alliances to achieve progressive development. ccoalition alliances spanned various fields such as: a. Coalition 4 Social Justice & Socio-economic rights led by CPA, involving 8 organisations; b. Alliance for Active Citizenship & Responsive Municipalities led by SiV, involving 4 organisations; c. Citizens alliance for transparency led by KDI, involving 10 organisations and d. Outlook on Local Elections led by D Plus, involving 16 organisations. Among other things, the individual projects implemented are: Advancing socio-economic rights by Qendra Multimedia, Digitalisation for overcoming language barriers by NGO AKTIV, Transparency of municipal administrations by YAHR, Workers rights in the call centre sector by SOTK, Legal assistance by Airport Union, Membership campaigns by Tax Administration Union and Internal capacity building by IPKO.
In 2022, the focus has been on strengthening capabilities and creating alliances and, among other things, the following have been achieved:
- The Coalition 4 Social Justice has put all necessary administrative and financial mechanisms in place for a long-term cooperation, has adequate executive structures, management positions and internal policies governing their operations including policies on gender equality, transparency and environmental aspects. In addition has drafted and adopted a five-year strategy and established long-term projects with other donors to ensure sustainability.
The Coalition 4 Social Justice engaged in a permanent dialogue with Kosovo's Ministry of Finance, Labour and Transfers regarding important issues such as parental leave, collective agreements, health and safety in the workplace, and the Labour Law. It was was directly involved in the drafting process of laws and regulations in the field of labour, including collective bargaining, Law on labour inspectorate, Law on health and safety, in cooperation with the Ministry of Finance, Labour and Finance, Department of Labour Relations Social Dialogue, Health, and Safety at Work.
As a way of expanding their legitimacy, the Coalition 4 Social Justice gathered gathered opinions from more than 15 000 workers from the police and health sector in a structured needs assessment at the beginning of the year that was used to build activities during the rest of the year.
- The KDI led Citizens alliance for transparency consolidated its internal financial control and management policies based on the strategic plan for 2020- 2024 guaranteeing transparency, accountability and gender equality, sexual harassment policies at work place, internal whistleblowing policies and grades and salaries are transparent to employees, citizens, and other relevant institutions.
- The Democracy Coalition for Outlook for local elections further developed their monitoring methodology and tools to follow-up on the commitments made by winning mayors and political parties in the past municipal elections. In addition to the work with the alliances and coalitions, OPC focused on supporting institutional capacities of various trade unions such as SPPI Sindikatae pavarur e puntoreve te IPKO, Trade Union Association Prishtina International Airport 'Adem Jashari', Trade Union of employees of Tax Administration and SOTK - Union of Telephone Operators of Kosovo. They all got support to update internal procedures on finance, management and steering documents including special trainings on gender awareness. IPKO union developed a mobile application that enables members to inform on labour rights violations and receive relevant guidance on how to act in the workplace. The application is also used for internal elections, increasing the level of democracy and transparency and IPKO has shared their model with other trade unions.
The Union of Prishtina International Airport increased its membership from 200 to 600 members and now has almost 90% unionization at the airport. Thanks to the union's efforts and the legal aid provided through the OPC project, 60 previously fired workers were able to return to their positions after court decisions.
- NGO AKTIV and members of the Empirika platform facilitated communication between citizens and public institutions such as the Ombudsperson and the Consultative Committee for Communities, also by using various digital mechanisms to engage a broader range of citizen groups concerning non-majority communities rights. The Aber mobile application created and developed by NGO AKTIV was critical in empowering citizens and advancing their rights and facilitated the dialogue with public institutions. However, local institutions in the Serb-majority municipalities have been unresponsive, mainly due to the withdrawal of Kosovo Serbs from central and some local level institutions.
- The Citizens alliance for transparency developed a methodology for monitoring local government budget hearings, enhancing their capacities in relation to participatory budgeting issues. Also the Transparency Index developed by the alliance is now an established and well recognized tool for monitoring municipal transparency.
Supporting coalitions, alliances and networks has been the main focus of the OPC, enabling effective cooperation, information exchange and coordinated action towards common objectives and in this regard below are some examples of this work from 2022:
- YAHR from Lipjan established a new alliance for the Local Development Initiative in the Municipality of Fushë Kosovë, partnering with NGO Academy in the Municipality of Shtime and Shales Youth Vision for the Municipality of Lipjan. - The Coalition 4 Social Justice strengthened the partnership with the Labour Inspectorate and trade unions through sharing of data on relevant issues. The Coalition also expanded its regional work through collaborations with organisations from North Macedonia, Albania and Serbia, sharing best practices and taking joint action on common issues such as a regional labour market. - The Alliance 4 Active Citizenship & Responsive Municipalities provided valuable capacity building opportunities to the partner CSD and its work among the Serbian community in Kosovo. By working together as a strong alliance, CSD was able to establish itself as a prominent player in the field.
- The D Coalition for Outlook for local elections expanded to cover more municipalities and the total number of engaged organisations grew to 16. The Coalition also participated in regional workshops organized by the POP Network in Albania and INFO Centar in North Macedonia, where partners shared their experiences and lessons learned regarding citizen engagement and institutional accountability and responsiveness in the context of municipal elections.
- KDI partnered with four Transparency International chapters from the region (North Macedonia, Montenegro, Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina), to implement project aimed to provide free legal expertise to citizens in order to combat corruption. The established Advocacy and Legal Advice Centres (ALACs) will work to strengthen the institutional framework for fighting corruption, including whistleblowing at national and regional levels.
Empirika platform and NGO AKTIV successfully developed informal coalitions and associations with citizens from non-majority backgrounds, eenabling them to coordinate and direct advocacy with public institutions such as the Deputy Minister for Communities, Consultative Committee for Communities and Ministry for Communities and Return. The platform also engaged in consultative communication with international stakeholders like OSCE and EULEX to address issues related to non-majority communities' interests.
In 2022, one of the main topics covered in the continued efforts to strengthen networking between trade unions and CSOs, was related to incorporating gender components in internal procedures of the Police Union, the Health Workers Union, the Union of Prishtina Airport, the Tax Authority union, IPKO Union and SOTK.
